A 5W power-amplifier for ultra-broad-band applications
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of high-efficiency power amplifiers for ultra-broadband operation.
the design of a 5W broadband power amplifier for ultra-broadband wireless communications.
the development of a power amplifier that is capable of delivering a broadband power of 5W at a frequency range of 2-500MHz.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power amplifier is capable of achieving a broadband power gain of 22±0.5dB with a power-added efficiency in excess of 43% from 2 to more than 500MHz.
the presented power amplifier exhibits the best performance among the power amplifiers for the ultra-b broad-band reported to date.
this is the first time that the design and implementation of a 5W ultra broadband power amplifier using silicon technology has been reported.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the power amplifier presented in this paper is a good candidate to replace the conventional vacuum-tube power amplifiers for ultra-broadband wireless communications.

we have successfully designed and implemented a power amplifier which can provide the high output power and the power-added efficiency required, as well as the broadband operation required for a variety of wireless applications.
a power amplifier using silicon devices has been designed to operate over a frequency range that is more than 1000 times wider than the frequency range that has been previously reported.

the presented power amplifier is a promising candidate for the ultra-breadband applications such as radar and wireless communications systems.
it is possible to implement a high-efficiency, high-power amplifier with ultra-wideband performance using a single-stage power amplifier topology using silicon LDMOsFETs.
